spike: Ruby 3.1.7 → 4.0.9 directly on main (Rails 7.0.10), time-boxed; findings only, not a phase
base_commit: 636918b (main: CI: publish Docker images only from main (#222))
why_a_spike: upgrade_path.json (PR #221) schedules Ruby 3.1 → 3.4 as Phase 13 (after Rails 7.2) and Ruby 3.4 → 4.0 as Phase 18 (after Rails 8.1 and haml 7). Rails 7.0.10 is not a supported Rails release on Ruby 4.0, there is no ruby:4.0-slim-bookworm image (Ruby 4.0 images are Trixie only), and Ruby 4.0 ships RubyGems 4 / Bundler 4. This spike does the mechanical jump anyway to see what actually breaks. Nothing here is meant to merge.

environment_observed_in_ruby_4_0_9_slim_.bundler_shipped_with_ruby: 4.0.20 (default gem). The brief assumed 4.0.23; 4.0.23 is the newest on rubygems.org (2026-10-14) but the image ships 4.0.20, so 4.0.20 is what the Dockerfiles pin

environment_observed_in_ruby_4_0_9_slim_.local_arch: arm64 (aarch64-linux); CI (x86_64) was not exercised locally

Dockerfile.base / Dockerfile.development.from: ruby:3.1.7-slim-bookworm → ruby:4.0.9-slim-trixie (forced: no 4.0 Bookworm tag; this collapses plan Phases 13, 14 and 18 into one FROM change, which is exactly why the plan keeps them apart)
Dockerfile.base / Dockerfile.development.apt: dropped ruby-dev (installs Debian's own Ruby headers, not the image's); build-essential patch zlib1g-dev liblzma-dev libpq-dev curl unchanged and all exist on Trixie
Dockerfile.base / Dockerfile.development.nodesource: setup_20.x → setup_26.x. The 26.x channel publishes a single `nodistro` suite, so it installs on Trixie without a Trixie-specific repo; nodejs 26.12.1-1nodesource1 was installed. setup_24.x fallback was not needed. Phase 6 does the same bump on Bookworm separately
Dockerfile.base / Dockerfile.development.nokogiri_preinstall: gem install nokogiri -v 1.18.10 → 1.19.4 (newest 1.19; precompiled aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-linux-gnu gems exist; 1.18.x precompiled gems declare ruby >= 3.1, < 3.5.dev). NOTE: this line only matches the bundle if Gemfile.lock also says 1.19.4 — see forced_gem_moves.nokogiri

changes_made..circleci/config.yml: cimg/ruby:3.1-node → cimg/ruby:4.0-node (tag existence taken from the brief, not verified locally; CI will tell)
changes_made.Dockerfile.ci / scripts/docker_build.rb: UNTOUCHED on purpose. Dockerfile.ci is FROM automationcalculationsci/automation-calculator-base:0.7.0, a Ruby 3.1.7 / Bookworm image. CI's `./go build ci` will therefore run `bundle install --frozen` with this Bundler 4 lockfile on Ruby 3.1.7 and fail (bundler 4.0.20, nokogiri 1.19.4 and minitest 6.0.6 all require Ruby >= 3.2). A real version of this change needs a new base image tag built from the new Dockerfile.base and pushed to Docker Hub for both arches — that is Phase 6/13 territory and was deliberately not done in a spike
changes_made..rubocop.yml: LEFT at TargetRubyVersion 3.1. rubocop 1.28.2 rejects 4.0 in the project config: `Error: RuboCop found unknown Ruby version 4.0 in TargetRubyVersion parameter (in .rubocop.yml). Supported versions: 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 3.0, 3.1, 3.2`. (Quirk worth knowing: the same config passed via `rubocop -c <path>` skips that validation and lints 160 files 'cleanly' — do not trust a `-c` run as proof.) Phase 10 (rubocop 1.9x) is the prerequisite for any TargetRubyVersion above 3.2, including Phase 13's 3.4
changes_made.Gemfile: gem 'pg', '~> 1.5.0' → '~> 1.7' (the only Gemfile change). No `gem 'ostruct'` was needed: config 5.6.1 already declares ostruct as a runtime dependency and ostruct 0.6.3 is in the lock. No `gem 'tsort'` needed yet (warning only, see warnings). `platforms: %w[mri mingw x64_mingw]` on byebug left as-is but Bundler 4 now prints `[DEPRECATED] Platform :mingw, :x64_mingw will be removed in the future. Please use platform :windows instead.` on every bundler command
changes_made.Gemfile.lock: regenerated with Bundler 4.0.20 using targeted `bundle lock --update <gem>` runs only (no blanket update). 33 changed lines. PLATFORMS still aarch64-linux, ruby, x86_64-linux. BUNDLED WITH 2.4.22 → 4.0.20 (full patch level kept; indentation changed from three spaces to two). No CHECKSUMS section was added — Bundler 4 only writes one for brand-new lockfiles or after `bundle lock --add-checksums`; an existing lockfile is left alone

build_attempts.what: Dockerfile.development on ruby:4.0.9-slim-trixie with main's Gemfile + Gemfile.lock (BUNDLED WITH 2.4.22)
build_attempts.apt_nodesource_nokogiri_bundler_steps: all succeeded (apt on Trixie, NodeSource 26.x, nokogiri 1.19.4 precompiled in 0.6s, bundler 4.0.20)
build_attempts.first_thing_seen: `Bundler 4.0.20 is running, but your lockfile was generated with 2.4.22. Installing Bundler 2.4.22 and restarting using that version.` — Bundler's self-management downgraded to the lockfile's version, so the install actually ran under bundler 2.4.22 on Ruby 4.0. Bumping BUNDLED WITH (or running `bundle lock` first) is required before Bundler 4 is really in play
build_attempts.failure: byebug 10.0.2: `context.c:190:20: error: passing argument 1 of 'rb_ensure' from incompatible pointer type [-Wincompatible-pointer-types]` (and arg 3, and anyargs.h rb_define_singleton_method_01) → `make failed, exit code 2` → `An error occurred while installing byebug (10.0.2), and Bundler cannot continue.` GCC 14 (Trixie) promotes -Wincompatible-pointer-types to an error; this would also hit a Ruby 3.4-on-Trixie build (Phase 14) if byebug 10 were still locked then — Phase 13 moves it to 13 first, so the plan order is right
build_attempts.note: Bundler's parallel installer aborts on the first failure, so this log says nothing about the other native gems; see native_gem_probe

build_attempts.what: after `bundle lock --update pg byebug` under Bundler 4.0.20 (BUNDLED WITH bumped by hand first)
build_attempts.result: image built; `bundle install` printed `Resolving dependencies...` and `Bundle complete! 42 Gemfile dependencies, 167 gems`
build_attempts.hidden_problem: the lockfile baked into the image differed from the host's: minitest 5.17.0 → 6.0.6 (+ drb ~> 2.0, prism ~> 1.5). minitest 5.17.0 declares required_ruby_version `>= 2.6, < 4.0`, so Bundler 4 silently auto-unlocked it at install time on Ruby 4.0 (a throwaway `bundle lock` run does not materialise against the running Ruby and had kept 5.17.0). Consequence: anything that then used the host lockfile failed with `Could not find minitest-5.17.0 in locally installed gems (Bundler::GemNotFound)` at `require 'bundler/setup'`, and a `bundle install --frozen` (Dockerfile.ci / Dockerfile.production) would refuse outright

build_attempts.result: image built, no re-resolution; `rspec` loaded and ran green (see suite_results)

build_attempts.what: after `bundle lock --update nokogiri` (1.18.10 → 1.19.4) so the lock matches the Dockerfile pre-install
build_attempts.result: image built; 166 gems; nokogiri 1.19.4 reused from the pre-install step instead of compiling libxml2 from source as 1.18.10 had been doing (its precompiled gem is gated `< 3.5.dev`)

native_gem_probe.method: `gem install <name> -v <locked version> --platform ruby` for every native gem in main's lockfile, one at a time, in a fresh ruby:4.0.9-slim-trixie container with build-essential libpq-dev libyaml-dev zlib1g-dev
compile_ok_at_locked_version: pg 1.5.9 (compiles; runtime on 4.0 not tested because it was moved anyway)
nokogiri 1.18.10 (from source, ~34s with -j15; the precompiled gem is rejected on 4.0)
compile_failed_at_locked_version: byebug 10.0.2 (GCC 14 incompatible-pointer-types errors, see attempt 1); byebug 13.0.0 compiles

pg.to: 1.7.0 (+ 1.7.0-aarch64-linux and 1.7.0-x86_64-linux platform gems now in the lock)
pg.why: Gemfile constraint bumped per the brief; 1.7.0 declares ruby >= 3.1, < 4.1 and ships precompiled linux gems, so it no longer links against the image's libpq at build time at all (Phase 14's libpq-17 note becomes moot for pg; libpq-dev is still needed only for a source fallback). 1.5.9 did in fact compile on 4.0.9 in the probe, so this was a chosen move, not a resolver-forced one

byebug.why: 10.0.2 fails to compile under GCC 14 (see attempt 1). 13.0.0 requires ruby >= 3.2 and compiled and loaded fine; the plan's Phase 18 fallback to `debug` was not needed

pry.why: 0.12.2 raises at load: `NameError: undefined method '=~' for class 'Pry::Code'` (pry/code.rb:338 undef_method :=~; Object#=~ was removed in Ruby 3.2). spec_helper.rb requires pry first, so the whole suite died with `0 examples, 1 error occurred outside of examples`. This is a Ruby >= 3.2 break, i.e. it belongs on Phase 13's list, not just Phase 10's 'patch/minor bumps'

minitest.why: 5.17.0 declares `< 4.0`. Bundler auto-unlocks it in a non-frozen install (attempt 2) but a frozen one fails; locked explicitly so host and image agree. Rails 7.0.10 (activesupport minitest >= 5.1) accepted 6.0.6 and rspec-rails' minitest adapters loaded

nokogiri.why: 1.18.10's precompiled gems are `>= 3.1, < 3.5.dev`; on 4.0 Bundler falls back to a source build of libxml2 even though the Dockerfile pre-installs 1.19.4. 1.19 requires ruby >= 3.2 (Phase 13 already planned this move)

conclusion.summary: Mechanically, Ruby 4.0.9 + Rails 7.0.10 is green on this codebase on arm64: image builds, rubocop clean (at TargetRubyVersion 3.1), rspec 366/0/6, assets:precompile OK, app boots, with five lockfile moves (pg, byebug, pry, minitest, nokogiri) and one Gemfile constraint change. The 'red' is structural rather than in the suite: CI cannot pass because Dockerfile.ci builds FROM the Ruby 3.1.7 base image 0.7.0 and the Bundler 4 lockfile cannot be installed there; rubocop 1.28 cannot target 4.0; and Rails 7.0.10 on Ruby 4.0 is unsupported upstream (it works here because this app touches little of Rails, not because Rails 7.0 is 4.0-safe — Rails only shipped 4.0 fixes in 8.0.4.1+/8.1.3+ and 7.0 receives no patches of any kind).
must_land_first: Phase 6 — Node 26 and the base-image bump workflow (new automation-calculator-base tag, Dockerfile.ci / docker_build.rb / docker_hub.rb)
Phase 10 — rubocop 1.9x (TargetRubyVersion > 3.2), pry/byebug/annotate/database_cleaner/shoulda-matchers/simplecov catch-up; pry must be explicitly bumped here or in 13
Phase 11 — Rails 7.1 (removes the 119 URI::RFC3986_PARSER warnings, secrets → secret_key_base)
Phase 13 — Ruby 3.4 with its own base image tag (nokogiri 1.19, bundler 2.7, Ruby-gated test gems; the only step on this spike's list that is 'free' because 3.4 keeps Bookworm)
Phase 14 — Trixie, with its own base image tag (GCC 14 C-extension exposure is isolated here)
Phase 15 and 16 — Rails 8.0 → 8.1.3+ (the first Rails lines that are actually tested on Ruby 4.0)

Phase 17 — haml 7 is not required by Ruby 4.0 on this evidence (haml 5.2.2 ran the whole suite without a single warning), but it remains the right time to do it before 18 so regressions stay attributable
conclusion.then_phase_18: Ruby 4.0.x + Bundler 4: bump BUNDLED WITH first (or run `bundle lock` under Bundler 4) so Bundler does not downgrade itself; expect only the Bundler 4 lockfile mechanics plus whatever Ruby-4.0-gated gems remain at that point; keep `bundle install --frozen` builds in the loop because a non-frozen install hides Ruby-version-gated lock entries (minitest here)
conclusion.reusable_from_this_spike: the Dockerfile diff (FROM, ruby-dev removal, setup_26.x, nokogiri/bundler pins) is exactly Phase 14 + 18's Dockerfile content; the lockfile moves for pry and nokogiri are Phase 13's; pg ~> 1.7 can be taken any time
